newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain debt held by foreigners down.
newsitem.headline: Spain debt held by foreigners down.

text.p: Spain's debt held by foreign residents dropped by 1.80 trillion pesetas to 3.62 trillion pesetas in the week ended on February 28, the Bank of Spain said on Tuesday.
It added notes and bonds fell to 3.57 trillion pesetas from previous 5.37 trillion pesetas, while short-term bills rose to 53.3 billion pesetas from 48 one week earlier.

Experts cautioned that a large part of this movement was due to so-called coupon washing, in which dealers sell bonds to foreigners with a better fiscal treatment when they have to cash in interest payments. Then they buy the bond back.
The previous week, to February 21, Spanish public debt in foreigners' hands rose to 606 billion pesetas.
At the end of February one year ago the public debt held by non-residents fell by 1.3 trillion pesetas.
